The Society

SeaBrick Society

A Canadian not-for-profit corporation, formed in 2022, whose purpose is to promote innovation and standards around environmentally sustainable marine infrastructure building materials.

17 February 2022Incorporated under the Canada Not-for-profit Corporations Act
1378929-2Corporation number, Corporations Canada; registered extraprovincially in British Columbia
VancouverRegistered office in British Columbia, Canada

Purpose

To promote innovation and standards around environmentally sustainable marine infrastructure building materials.

The articles of incorporation also provide that the Society is carried on without the purpose of gain for its members, that any profits are used to further its purposes, that directors serve without remuneration, and that on dissolution any remaining property is distributed to qualified donees.

Governance

The Society has one class of members, each entitled to notice of, attendance at and a vote at members' meetings. It is governed by a board of between one and ten directors, elected by the members, who serve without pay. Its financial year ends on 31 December and it files annual returns with Corporations Canada.

Relationship to other organisations

Commercial development of SeaBrick, including early fundraising, manufacturing trials and the kelp supply chain, has been carried by Kelp Island Inc., a related company formed in 2021. BioLith is the Society's commercial partner for production of SeaBrick and for other uses of the mineral-foam and fibre material now in development. The Society's role in each case is the same: to hold the standard and the public research record, and to make sure what is learned is available to anyone who wants to build with the system.

Not a registered charity. SeaBrick Society is a not-for-profit corporation, not a registered charity under the Income Tax Act. It does not issue charitable donation receipts, does not sell shares or memberships with financial returns, and does not pay dividends.

Get involved

Researchers and students. Materials, marine engineering, naval architecture, life-cycle assessment. There is a long list of questions and a short list of people.

Coastal communities and partners. If you need working infrastructure on the water, a float, a platform, a dock, and would consider a pilot, we would like to talk.

Builders and makers. The model bricks exist so that people can try the system. Open days and workshops are announced in the journal.

Contact the Society

Advisors and collaborators

Over five years the project has drawn on materials engineers, marine engineers, an ocean architect, seaweed scientists, climate strategists and business advisors, as well as UBC faculty and more than thirty engineering students. Their contributions are credited in the journal articles that describe the work.
